provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Body changes talk
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to state body changes.
The pupils should be able to ask questions about growing.
Introduction:
We all grow every day.
Our bodies change as we grow.
Content:
Growing up means getting bigger.
Hair grows longer.
We get taller.
Our teeth change.
We can ask questions about our bodies.
The teacher shows pictures of children at different ages.
Class activity:
Stand up and stretch high.
Touch your toes.
Count how many times you can jump.
Evaluation questions:
What happens when you grow?
Name one body change.
Can you ask a question about growing?
Summary:
Growing up is healthy and natural.

topics.title: Personal safety plan
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to list safe adults.
The pupils should be able to remember their phone number.
Introduction:
We need to be safe every day.
Some adults help us stay safe.
Content:
Safe adults are parents, teachers, police.
We can tell safe adults our problems.
Our phone number helps us call home.
We practice saying our phone number.
The teacher shows pictures of safe community helpers.
Class activity:
Make a safe adults list with drawings.
Practice saying your phone number with a friend.
Evaluation questions:
Who is a safe adult?
What is your phone number?
Why do we need safe adults?
Summary:
Know your safe adults and phone number.

topics.title: Emergency numbers
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify emergency numbers.
The pupils should be able to role-play calling for help.
Introduction:
Sometimes we need help fast.
Special numbers help us in emergencies.
Content:
Police is 112.
Ambulance is 112.
Fire service is 112.
We can call these numbers when there is danger.
We say our name and where we are.
The teacher shows a big phone with emergency numbers.
Class activity:
Pretend to call 112.
Say your name and address clearly.
Take turns being the caller and helper.
Evaluation questions:
What number do you call for police?
What do you say when you call for help?
Can you role-play an emergency call?
Summary:
Know emergency numbers and how to ask for help.

topics.title: Sports and teamwork
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to play relay games.
The pupils should be able to explain fair play.
Introduction:
Sports are fun with friends.
Working together makes games better.
Content:
Relay games need teams.
Pass the baton without dropping it.
Ball games need sharing and taking turns.
Fair play means following rules.
We cheer for everyone.
The teacher demonstrates a simple relay race.
Class activity:
Play a relay race with batons.
Play a simple ball passing game.
Clap for each other after the game.
Evaluation questions:
What is a relay race?
Why is teamwork important?
What does fair play mean?
Summary:
Play fair and work together in sports.

topics.title: Rest and relaxation
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to practice quiet time.
The pupils should be able to do simple breathing exercises.
Introduction:
Playing all day can make us tired.
Rest helps our bodies and minds relax.
Content:
Quiet time means sitting still and calm.
Deep breathing helps us relax.
We can count to five when breathing in and out.
Quiet time makes us feel better.
The teacher leads a quiet time session.
Class activity:
Sit quietly for two minutes.
Practice deep breathing together.
Count five breaths in and five breaths out.
Evaluation questions:
What is quiet time?
How does breathing help us relax?
Why do we need rest?
Summary:
Rest and breathing help us feel calm.

topics.title: Screen health
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to list screen time rules.
The pupils should be able to demonstrate good posture.
Introduction:
Phones and tablets can be fun.
Too much screen time hurts our eyes and body.
Content:
Too much screen time makes eyes tired.
Sit straight when using screens.
Take breaks every 20 minutes.
Family media plan helps limit screen time.
The teacher shows pictures of good and bad screen posture.
Class activity:
Practice good screen posture.
Set a timer for 20 minutes.
Do eye exercises when the timer rings.
Evaluation questions:
Why should we limit screen time?
What is good screen posture?
How often should we take breaks?
Summary:
Take care of your eyes and body when using screens.

topics.title: Growing food
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to water plants.
The pupils should be able to name one vegetable.
Introduction:
Food comes from plants.
We can help plants grow in our school garden.
Content:
Plants need water to grow.
We can plant seeds in soil.\Vegetables like tomatoes and carrots grow from plants.
We can harvest and taste what we grow.
The teacher shows real plants and seeds.
Class activity:
Water the school garden plants.
Plant seeds in small cups.
Taste a simple vegetable if available.
Evaluation questions:
What do plants need to grow?
Name one vegetable we can grow.
How do we help plants grow?
Summary:
Water plants and watch them grow into food.

topics.title: Health careers
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to name health helpers.
The pupils should be able to ask health helpers questions.
Introduction:
Many people help us stay healthy.
We can learn about their jobs.
Content:
Doctors help when we are sick.
Nurses give medicine and care.
Pharmacists give us medicine from the shop.
We can ask them questions about health.
The teacher invites a health worker if possible.
Class activity:
Draw a picture of a health helper.
Practice asking health questions like "Why do we wash hands?"
Evaluation questions:
What does a doctor do?
Who gives us medicine at the pharmacy?
What question would you ask a health helper?
Summary:
Health helpers keep us strong and healthy.

topics.title: My health promise
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to choose healthy habits.
The pupils should be able to make a health promise.
Introduction:
We can promise to take care of ourselves.
Healthy habits make us strong and happy.
Content:
Healthy habits include washing hands, eating fruits, sleeping well.
We pick three habits to keep every day.
We sign our promise to remember.
The teacher shows examples of health promises.
Class activity:
Draw three healthy habits you want to keep.
Sign your health promise paper.
Share one habit with the class.
Evaluation questions:
What is a health promise?
Name one healthy habit.
Why should we keep our health promises?
Summary:
Make and keep your health promises.

topics.title: Revision and health graduation
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to teach a health habit.
The pupils should be able to receive a health award.
Introduction:
We learned many health habits this term.
Today we celebrate our health knowledge.
Content:
We teach friends what we learned.
Health ambassadors help others stay healthy.
We get awards for trying our best.
The teacher gives out simple health certificates.
Class activity:
Teach a health habit to a partner.
Receive your health ambassador award.
Clap for all health ambassadors.
Evaluation questions:
What health habit will you teach?
Why are we health ambassadors?
What did you learn about health this term?
Summary:
Celebrate being a health ambassador.
